clue.text: Extremely unfavourable outcome of engagement later quashed in court

indicators.note: the crushed word sits inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: something quashed is crushed out of shape, so the word before it loses its order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A battle lost, then a later legal verdict overturned in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' reads as a betrothal or a court case here, but it is a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final defeat gave English the phrase 'to meet one's Waterloo', meaning a decisive, crushing loss in a contest.

clue.text: Meat-eater heard greeting moralist in The Street?

indicators.note: what is heard is the spoken form, so the words that follow are judged by their sound

parts.note: hi is a greeting; Ena Sharples was the stern moral watchdog of Coronation Street

explanation.surface: A carnivore overheard saying hello to a prim neighbour in a street.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap, often just 'The Street'; Ena Sharples was its disapproving gossip. Saying 'Hi, Ena' gives the animal's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyaena is a carnivorous African mammal that hunts and scavenges flesh, so it is a classic flesh-eating animal.

clue.text: Infidels present during more than one robbery

parts.note: being present at an event, or at a time, is being there during it
a heist is a robbery, and more than one makes it plural

explanation.surface: Unbelievers were on the scene for a series of robberies.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidels are people without religious faith, and those who deny that any god exists are nonbelievers of the strongest kind.

clue.text: Bit of a boob leaving top actor speechless? Work stops now

indicators.note: leaving its top means the first letter of the word below goes away

parts.note: a teat is the nipple, a part of a breast
a mime is an actor who performs without words

explanation.surface: An actor's wardrobe slip leaves them lost for words; time to down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the afternoon break for tea traditionally halts work for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition describes the moment rather than naming it: the afternoon tea break is the point in the day when labour pauses.

clue.text: Author who provides fuels from gas to kerosene
City man is about to crack cryptic link

parts.note: he is a male person

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the little word is to be read the other way
to crack something is to break into it, so one piece gets in between the letters of the other
something cryptic is jumbled and obscure, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is about to break a cryptic connection, like a codebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland, a major Nordic port and urban centre on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Poor Ireland, endlessly under discussion

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of the country is cut
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are left out of their proper order

parts.note: the country without its last letter

explanation.surface: Ireland's sorry plight is still being argued over.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means literally 'in the air', which in English is a way of saying undecided and still being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up in the air is unresolved and still being debated, which is what this French borrowing conveys.

clue.text: "Are we comfortable here?" Eaters set to reorder, apprehending Sally's climax …

definitions.note: a question pointing at a place, where the answer is a noun phrase

indicators.note: apprehending means catching and holding, so the rearranged letters hold the single letter
to reorder is to set out again in a different sequence, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the climax is the end point, so only the closing letter of the name is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Diners in Katz's Deli, as in When Harry Met Sally, ask if they are comfy while ordering again around Sally's famous fake climax.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue: the scene is the restaurant in When Harry Met Sally, where Sally fakes an orgasm and a diner orders what she's having.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on easy street is an idiom for a life of comfort and affluence, so it is where you would be at your ease.

clue.text: … a long time doing the same — people do in Katz's

indicators.note: doing the same refers back to the previous clue, where only a word's climax, its final letter, was used

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Diners in Katz's spend ages copying Sally, ordering what she's having.
explanation.walkthrough: In the film, a woman nearby says 'I'll have what she's having' after Sally's display, which is people doing the same in Katz's Deli, New York.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period, and the plural is used loosely for ages or a very lengthy stretch.

clue.text: Intense medical examiner keeps males fit!

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a vet medically examines animals, and to vet is to examine
he-men are fit, strong, muscular males

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic doctor approves male patients as fit for duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medical examiner' suggests a doctor for people, but the examiner here treats animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement feelings or arguments are forceful and passionate, the same strength of feeling as intense.

clue.text: I'm disgusted with king because of fortress

parts.note: K is the chess notation for king
as can mean because, as in 'as it was late'
bah is an exclamation of disgust or contempt

explanation.surface: Someone disgusted with a king because of his stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A kasbah is the citadel of a North African city, with the old quarter around a fortified castle.

clue.text: Continually breaking law, say?

indicators.note: breaking smashes the words apart so their letters can be put together differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who is forever getting on the wrong side of the law, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something always means doing it all the time without stopping, the same sense as continually.

clue.text: Something saucy slipped back into Tony's song

indicators.note: into means placed inside the following word

parts.note: in West Side Story Tony sings Maria, about his beloved

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: a stocking that has slipped a stitch has ran, or laddered; to slip off is also to run

explanation.surface: A risqué line was sneaked into a song from a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something saucy' sounds like innuendo, but it is literally a sauce. Tony is the hero of West Side Story.
explanation.definitionFit: Marinara is an Italian tomato, garlic and herb sauce served with pasta, so it is literally a thing that is a sauce.

clue.text: Rubbish defender's howler was doubly hard to comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to take in, so the outer letters take in another piece

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard, used twice, one at each end
a defender's worst error is an own goal, OG in match reports
taken as written

explanation.surface: A defender's blunder was baffling to understand, a load of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: One hard letter goes at each end, with the defender's error placed just inside the front one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash was originally swill fed to pigs, and now means nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Leave, celebrating late equaliser?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go away, pull out

definitions.note: a cryptic reading of the answer as two words: pleased with a draw
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split into two words: a last-minute goal leaves a team happy with a drawn result

explanation.surface: A football fan leaving the ground while celebrating a last-gasp equaliser.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is whimsical: a team that scores late to level is happy to end up with a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to pull back or depart from a place or contest, the same as to leave.

clue.text: Peter in film that anyone can see? He maybe has time for all like him?

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for a universal audience
Peter was a saint, so he is an example of a ST
1 November is All Saints' Day, a feast for all saints

explanation.surface: An actor who would watch a family film and make time for anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like the subject of 'He', but He stands for Saint Peter; 1 Nov is written I NOV.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Ustinov was a British actor, writer and raconteur, famous for films such as Spartacus and Death on the Nile.

clue.text: Bit by bit, perimetrically referenced woman contains rising passion

indicators.note: contains means one piece holds another within it

parts.note: the woman named in the clues around the grid's edge

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, the reverse of the normal direction

parts.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion

explanation.surface: A woman, gradually and from all sides, holds in a growing anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman is named in the clues for the entries around the edge of the grid, such as the Katz's Deli pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done serially happen one after another in a series, piece by piece rather than all at once.

clue.text: Apt signs describe where GP stands on potassium put under table?

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw round, so these pieces go around another

parts.note: a doctor's surgery door may show In and Out signs
a GP is a doctor, abbreviated DR
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A doctor's notice on the surgery wall about drinking potassium solutions.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first part above the second, so potassium comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone under the table is to drink more alcohol than they can, leaving them unconscious or collapsed.

clue.text: Harry finally says "bye" now he has to do a round

definitions.text: he has to do a round

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and push about, so the letters get jostled into new order
finally keeps only the closing letter of the word next to it

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prince Harry says goodbye, as he has another round of duties to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, as in the prince or Harry of When Harry Met Sally, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsboy delivers papers to houses along a set route every morning, called his paper round.

clue.text: Support for old gamblers that may be sacked?

definitions.note: read as two words: a table for the card game loo
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split: a table for loo, an old card game played for money

explanation.surface: An old gambling table that might be ransacked by thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a card game popular for gambling in the 17th to 19th centuries, played at its own round table.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, so anything able to be pillaged or seized as booty fits.

clue.text: He holds forth on podium, unless heap of rocks is available?

parts.note: or can mean unless, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A speaker needs a platform unless there is a rocky outcrop to stand on.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop of rock in south-west England, a natural platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds forth delivers long speeches, which is what a public speaker does from a platform.

clue.text: Beginner in espionage needed to make these subtler!

definitions.note: stands for the answer, which with the extra letter could be rearranged

indicators.note: to make another word out of letters is to rearrange them into it
this letter is needed alongside the answer, so the bigger word is the answer plus it; take it away

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy-school lesson: a beginner needs to soften tactless outbursts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add E to the answer and rearrange to get SUBTLER, so take the E from SUBTLER and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Blurts are tactless outbursts, the very things a subtle spy would avoid, so 'these' refers to sudden careless utterances.

clue.text: Potato cake that's flipped and served with eggs

parts.note: roe is the eggs of fish

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the short phrase is read backwards

parts.note: that's means that is, written it's

explanation.surface: A potato pancake turned in the pan and served with eggs for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipped' fits the cooking surface so well it looks literal. The answer is the Swiss dish rösti, written with OE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a flat round cake.

clue.text: Sally goes about on a cycle

indicators.note: on a cycle means letters go round, moving from the front to the back

parts.note: to go is slang for to urinate
ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally goes round on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: PEESCA has its first two letters moved round to the end. 'Sally' looks like a name, but here it is a sortie or breakout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden rush out from a besieged place, a breakout, which is a getaway from confinement.

clue.text: Means to transport people out of Portugal and Austria

indicators.note: out of says the letters are taken from within the following run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second, and into the third

explanation.surface: A vehicle for travellers leaving Portugal and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, built to carry passengers.

clue.text: Barnacle Bill's parting reason for moving?

indicators.note: parting means splitting something in two, so one piece goes in the middle of the other
for moving means the letters are to be moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a/c, an account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Barnacle Bill the sailor explains why he is setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barnacle Bill' reads as the name of the sailor in the old song, but the two words are split: one is the definition, the other the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea acorn is an old name for an acorn barnacle, a shelled marine crustacean that clings to rocks and hulls.

clue.text: 9 letters returned? Not this one

definitions.note: a clause saying this letter is not among those nine

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the run of letters is read in the other direction

parts.note: A to I covers nine letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter checks whether the ninth answer's letters are reversible here.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9 across, but it is a count. The answer is a Greek letter, so it is not one of the Roman A to I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet, not of the Roman alphabet the nine letters come from.

clue.text: Essentially, actor's got very rich, having secured work playing The Tramp?

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the five

indicators.note: having secured means holding fast inside, so one piece is locked within another

parts.note: rolling in it means very wealthy
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An actor grew rich after landing the part of Chaplin's Tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tramp' suggests Charlie Chaplin's film character, but here a tramp is a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A trollop is a disreputable woman, so behaving as one, or acting the part of one, is trolloping.
